name: Pembrolizumab + CAPOX (Capecitabine / OXALIplatin), PD-L1 CPS-positive

biomarkers.PD_L1_CPS: positive (CPS at least 1; category 1 for CPS at least 5)
biomarkers.note: This pembrolizumab-plus-chemotherapy regimen (KEYNOTE-859 style) is for HER2-negative advanced disease with PD-L1 CPS at least 1 (category 1 recommendation for CPS at least 5). For HER2-positive disease the guideline instead adds trastuzumab plus pembrolizumab to chemotherapy for CPS at least 1 (KEYNOTE-811) - see gi-gastric-trastuzumab-chemo and note below. MMR or MSI (MSI-H/dMMR favors checkpoint therapy) and Claudin 18.2 are also tested. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Gastric Cancer v3.2026, Systemic Therapy and Principles of Biomarker Testing.

lineOfTherapy: first-line systemic therapy for HER2-negative, PD-L1 CPS-positive metastatic or unresectable gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: PD-L1 CPS at least 1 (category 1 for CPS at least 5); HER2-negative
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v3.2026, Systemic Therapy (guidelines/gastric.txt line 2012: fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin + pembrolizumab for PD-L1 CPS at least 1, category 1 for CPS at least 5); CPS threshold line 1882
v3.2026, Systemic Therapy for advanced disease (guidelines/gastric.txt lines 1882 to 2020)

drugs.name: Pembrolizumab

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: lines 233347 to 233349 (pembrolizumab simplified to a flat dose of 200 mg every 3 weeks or 400 mg every 6 weeks, up to 2 years)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., lines 233347 to 233349 (agent-level flat dosing). Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV flat on day 1 every 3 weeks (alternative 400 mg every 6 weeks), continued up to 2 years. This is the general PK-based flat dose, not a gastric-specific locator; the gastric CPS gate is from the guideline. Monitor for immune-related adverse events.

drugs.name: OXALIplatin

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: line 99169 (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1 every 3 weeks, gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., line 99169. OXALIplatin 130 mg/m2 IV on day 1, every 3 weeks (CAPOX backbone). Tall-man per ISMP.

drugs.name: Capecitabine

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: line 98868 (capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice a day for 14 days)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., line 98868. Capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 orally twice daily on days 1 to 14 (CAPOX backbone; this per-dose is the twice-daily dose). Fluorouracil is a source-stated fluoropyrimidine alternative. DPYD deficiency raises fluoropyrimidine toxicity risk; consider DPYD testing before first dose.

supportiveCare: Chemotherapy backbone modeled as CAPOX (q3w) to align with pembrolizumab every 3 weeks; the guideline permits a fluoropyrimidine (capecitabine or fluorouracil) plus oxaliplatin backbone.
DPYD: consider DPYD genotype or phenotype testing before the fluoropyrimidine; reduce or avoid on deficiency.
Immune-related adverse event monitoring for pembrolizumab (thyroid, hepatic, pulmonary, colitis, endocrinopathies).
Antiemetics: oxaliplatin-based, moderate emetic risk; prophylaxis per emetogenicity tier.
Pembrolizumab continued up to 2 years; chemotherapy per tolerance (metastatic, cycle number not fixed).

monitoring: immune-related toxicity screen (TSH/free T4, LFTs, glucose, cortisol as indicated) during pembrolizumab
renal function and peripheral neuropathy assessment before each cycle (OXALIplatin)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Hold pembrolizumab and manage with corticosteroids per immune-related adverse event guidance; obtain clinical review before rechallenge.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: lines 233347 to 233349 (pembrolizumab flat dose 200 mg every 3 weeks or 400 mg every 6 weeks, up to 2 years); line 99169 (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 day 1 every 3 weeks); line 98868 (capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily x14 days)

guideline.locator: Systemic Therapy: add a checkpoint inhibitor to first-line chemotherapy for PD-L1 CPS at least 1 (guidelines/gastric.txt line 1882); fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin + pembrolizumab for CPS at least 1, category 1 for CPS at least 5 (line 2012); HER2-positive alternative adds trastuzumab plus pembrolizumab (lines 2007 to 2009, KEYNOTE-811)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in HER2-negative, PD-L1 CPS-positive metastatic gastric and GEJ adenocarcinoma (KEYNOTE-859 style), with a CAPOX backbone chosen to align with the every-3-week pembrolizumab schedule. Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV flat every 3 weeks (or 400 mg every 6 weeks) is grounded to DeVita 12th ed. lines 233347 to 233349 (agent-level PK-based flat dosing, not a gastric-specific locator). The CAPOX backbone doses are grounded to DeVita: oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 day 1 (line 99169) and capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 orally twice daily days 1 to 14 (line 98868); fluorouracil is a source-stated fluoropyrimidine alternative. The biomarker gate (PD-L1 CPS at least 1, category 1 for CPS at least 5; HER2-negative) is grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Gastric Cancer v3.2026 (guidelines/gastric.txt lines 1882 and 2012); the HER2-positive alternative that adds trastuzumab plus pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-811, lines 2007 to 2009) is noted. MMR or MSI and Claudin 18.2 are tested. Metastatic intent, cycles not fixed (null); pembrolizumab up to 2 years. ISMP tall-man applied (OXALIplatin). DPYD screening flagged for the fluoropyrimidine; immune-related adverse event monitoring flagged for pembrolizumab. No field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
